svg.title: a freshly generated project passes its own quality gate — OSV checks dependencies where their owner can fix them
svg.text: a freshly generated project passes its own quality gate
Scenario: OSV checks dependencies where their owner can fix them

g.text: Given every framework tool in a generated project contains the same
vulnerable package
GitLab shows lodash 4.17.20 in the inherited CodeceptJS lockfile. The same vulnerable
fixture is present in every framework tool.
When the generated project's OSV scan leaves inherited tools to the
toolbox
GitLab shows the inherited job's OSV log: no package sources found and No issues found. The
vulnerable framework tools leave the project pipeline green.
Then the toolbox's OSV scan reports the same vulnerable framework tools
GitLab shows the OSV error and the vulnerable framework lockfiles. The toolbox's own scanner
configuration catches the tools it owns.
When the developer adds vulnerable dependencies in project-owned
locations
GitLab shows the same vulnerable package in .config/project-tool. The fixture is also added
at the repository root and in two other project-owned locations.
Then OSV reports every project-owned copy of the vulnerable package
GitLab shows the OSV error: lodash 4.17.20, advisory GHSA-35jh-r3h4-6jhm, and all four
project-owned lockfiles, including .config/project-tool/package-lock.json. This finding
blocks the inherited code:megalinter job.
When the developer updates the framework through Copier
GitLab shows version 1.0.1 after a real Copier update. Project settings and dependency files
survive.
Then OSV keeps the same ownership boundary after the update
GitLab shows the same OSV advisory and project lockfiles after the Copier update. These
project vulnerabilities still block the job.
When the developer removes the project dependency fixtures
The project fixtures have been removed. GitLab shows that the vulnerable inherited
CodeceptJS fixture is still there.
Then the project's empty OSV scan passes with a clear result
GitLab shows No issues found again. Only vulnerable framework tools remain, so the generated
project's pipeline succeeds.
